findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed there to be no signed employee health reporting agreements during inspection. PIC was made aware. An email copy of the employee health reporting agreements was sent and copies were printed and employees signed the agreements to correct this violation. Ensure that all employees have signed an employee health reporting agreements and they are kept on file for future inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed there to be no Norovirus clean up procedure available in the facility. PIC was informed and an email was sent to provide them with the norovirus clean up procedure. The Norovirus clean up procedure was printed and posted in the kitchen to correct the violation.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed raw chicken breast stored above ready to eat yogurt tubes in the fridge in the kitchen. Shell eggs were observed stored above milk and juice. PIC was made aware and education was conducted regarding proper storage order. Staff was instructed to move items to correct the violation. Inspector provided storage order hand out for future reference. Ensure that all food is stored to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed window cleaner and air freshener stored above food on the metal storage shelf in the kitchen. PIC was made aware and the incorrectly stored bottles were moved to the bottom shelf to correct the violation. Ensure that chemicals and other cleaner are stored so they do not contaminate food or food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]
